title: Establish eval sensitivity protocol for config and model rollouts
creator: Aisha Menon
description: Create a repeatable protocol that ties benchmarks and scoring changes (rubrics, LLM-as-judge, and confidence calibration) to config and model rollouts. Deliverables: a rubric specification, LLM-as-judge standard operating procedure, calibration mapping and thresholds, and automated gating rules for canary/circuit-breakers.
background: We frequently change serving config (batching, quantization profile, kernel algo) and swap model variants during rollouts. Current eval signals are brittle: judge model score drift and rubric sensitivity lead to noisy alerts or missed regressions. Past incidents (see links) show undetected quality drops after a quantization tweak. We need a standard approach that reduces false positives while catching user-facing regressions quickly.
goals: Define a concise multi-axis rubric that captures factuality, instruction-following, and hallucination propensity for our primary use cases
Standardize an LLM-as-judge pipeline with ensemble voting and score calibration against human labels
Specify delta thresholds and cohort-level sensitivity for config changes (e.g., quantization vs kernel swap)
Automate gating: canary pass/fail and rollout rollback triggers integrated with CI and Console
out_of_scope: Full rebuild of eval infra (we will reuse existing eval harness and data infra); deep model re-training guidance
success_metrics: Reduce noisy regression alerts by >=40% on rollout events (measured over next quarter)
Detect user-impacting regressions with >=90% recall on historical replayed incidents
End-to-end gating latency (eval -> decision) under 30 minutes for canary-sized cohorts
proposed_rubric_changes: Move from flat score to hierarchical rubric: Top-level pass/fail + three diagnostic axes (Factuality, Safety, Instruction-Following)
Each axis scored 0-100 with recommended prompt templates and anchor examples
Introduce cohort-specific weighting (e.g., production chat vs batch embed workflows)
llm_as_judge_protocol: Use three judge models: two diverse open models + a small calibrated Redwood-verified judge
Prompt engineering: fixed system instruction + 5-shot anchors drawn from gold set; provide explicit scoring rubric in prompt
Aggregate by median score and compute inter-judge variance; flag cases with high variance for human review
Store raw judge logits/scores to enable later recalibration and audit
calibration_plan: Collect a stratified gold set (N=2k) labeled by human raters across target cohorts
Fit a monotonic calibration mapping (isotonic regression) from judge ensemble score -> calibrated probability of failure
Define calibrated thresholds for: info (low confidence delta), caution (requires manual review), fail (automated rollback), with cohort-specific baselines
Recalibrate monthly or after major judge model upgrades
rollout_and_gate_plan: Canary: run eval harness on a 1-2% traffic mirror for 24h; evaluate calibrated metrics and cohort deltas
Gating rules: immediate rollback if calibrated fail rate increases >1.5x baseline and absolute delta >0.02 on primary metric; otherwise hold and require manual approval
Progressive rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 100% with guardrails at each step and automated stop on triggers
Integration: expose gate outcomes to Console and CI (GitHub Checks) with links to failing examples and judge traces
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-rollout cohort histograms, judge variance, calibrated pass-rate time series
Automated alerts: severity levels (info/caution/fail) and email/Slack routing to on-call and PM/Eng
Sampling: persist top 50 highest-confidence failures and 50 high-variance cases for human audit
Retention: keep judge inputs/outputs for 90 days to support audits and recalibration
implementation_tasks: Spec the hierarchical rubric and publish anchor examples (PM + Design)
Extend eval harness to run judge ensemble and save raw scores (Eng)
Build calibration microservice and store mapping in Config Service (Eng)
Create Console widgets for gate status, failing examples, and judge variance (Frontend)
Author gating rules and CI integration (DevOps + Eng)
Run historical replay across last 6 rollouts and tune thresholds (PM + Eng + SRE)
risks_and_mitigation: Judge model drift: mitigate via monthly recalibration and human-in-the-loop fallback
Overfitting to gold set: use stratified sampling and reserve a test holdout
Latency: large judge ensembles increase eval time; mitigate with smaller fast judge + async deeper analysis
False rollback risk: conservative thresholds and manual approval path for ambiguous cases
open_questions: What is the minimum gold set size for stable calibration per cohort? (current estimate: 2k)
Should weight certain failure types (safety) higher than others for automated rollback?
How frequently should we recalibrate after judge model version bumps? (proposed: monthly + post-upgrade)
